column1: 91               A Midsummer Night’s Dream           ACT 3. SC. 2

column3:
Then will two at once woo one. That must needs be sport alone. And those things do best please me That befall prepost’rously.
They Enter Lysander and Helena.

column2:
Why should you think that I should woo in scorn?
Scorn and derision never come in tears.                                          125

Look when I vow, I weep; and vows so born, In their nativity all truth appears.
How can these things in me seem scorn to you, Bearing the badge of faith to prove them true?

You do advance your cunning more and more.                                 130
When truth kills truth, O devilish holy fray!
These vows are Hermia’s. Will you give her o’er?
Weigh oath with oath, and you will nothing weigh.
Your vows to her and me, put in two scales,                                      135
Will even weigh, and both as light as tales.

LYSANDER
I had no judgment when to her I swore.
HELENA
Nor none, in my mind, now you give her o’er.
